name: The Best Italian-American Tomato Sauce
headnote: J. Kenji Lopez-Alt set out to build the long-cooked Italian-American red sauce that restaurants used to stake their reputations on, and spent dozens of tests getting there. He starts with good canned whole peeled plum tomatoes crushed by hand for a chunky body, and blooms knife-chopped garlic, dried oregano and pepper flakes in a mix of olive oil and butter, arguing that the butter emulsifies more readily and makes the sauce creamier while hand-chopped garlic is coarse enough not to scorch. Sweetness comes from a whole carrot and a halved onion simmered in the pot and fished out later rather than from sugar. His key move is finishing the pot in a 300F oven with the lid cracked for five to six hours, which lets the surface caramelize gently and evenly with little stirring; a few cups of reserved raw crushed tomato stirred in at the end restores fresh flavor, and a splash of fish sauce adds savoriness.
comment_digest: Several cooks report the reduction running faster than the recipe implies. One found his sauce nearly at paste stage after only three hours and had to add canned sauce to stretch it; another advises watching it closely and lowering the oven temperature as the liquid drops rather than trusting the full five-to-six-hour window, and notes that little visible bubbling early on is normal. One reviewer would hold back less raw tomato at the end, about two cups instead of three, because the full amount diluted the richness he had cooked all day for. The fish sauce draws the most substitution traffic: readers report soy sauce, soy plus Marmite, minced shiitake or MSG as alternatives, and one asks about miso. Other reported variations include an eight-hour sealed slow cooker, adding reduced red wine and sweet Italian sausage, and swapping small white peaches for the carrot.
flags: Most featured comments are cut off at 'Read More', so only the visible text was used. Several reviews carry 2026 dates. Vote counts are all zero, so nothing could be ranked by helpfulness.
